slides.headline: Best countertop garden for apartments
slides.subhead: Quiet, compact systems that fit a real kitchen — what to buy first for a studio or 1-bed.
slides.narration: Best countertop garden for apartments. The Sill Garden answer for a small apartment, without buying more equipment than you need.

slides.headline:
Match the setup
to your space.
slides.subhead: Light, noise, and spill risk matter more than pod count.
slides.narration: Start with usable space, daylight, and a tray that protects the rental surface. Then pick the smallest setup that still grows what you cook.

slides.headline:
Don't buy the
biggest kit first.
slides.subhead: Weak light is not a watering problem.
slides.narration: Skip the largest system until the plants prove they need it. Stretching stems usually mean more light, not more water.

slides.headline:
Start small.
Prove the routine.
slides.subhead: Start with a 3–6 pod countertop kit if you want herbs with almost no learning curve. Use a mason-jar Kratky setup if you want to spend under
slides.narration: Our verdict: Start with a 3–6 pod countertop kit if you want herbs with almost no learning curve. Use a mason-jar Kratky setup if you want to spend under $40 and learn the basics first. Full guide on Sill Garden dot com.
